author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Colby-Sawyer handed Keene State its first loss of the field-hockey season Saturday, winning 3-2 in New London on Abby Olden’s goal with 20 seconds left in the first half. The Chargers improved to 4-0, while the Owls fell to 4-1 after twice answering an earlier Colby-Sawyer lead.

Brooke Farquhar scored twice for the Chargers. Keene State responded through Henley Gilstrap and Lilah Carr, making it 2-2 before Olden converted from a penalty corner just before the break. The second half produced no goals, though the Owls generated sustained pressure late and forced goalkeeper Sophie Krauss into several important saves.

Keene State finished with a 15-12 edge in shots and a 14-7 advantage in penalty corners, including nine shots and seven corners in the fourth quarter. Krauss made six saves for Colby-Sawyer. Gilstrap’s goal was her team-leading seventh in five games. The Owls return home Wednesday to face Western New England.
dek: Abby Olden scored with 20 seconds left before halftime, and the Chargers survived a fourth-quarter push by the Owls.
headline: Late first-half goal lifts Colby-Sawyer past Keene State, 3-2
